correctness.rationale: The proof is sound. Stability at slope 5 forces every line subbundle to have degree at most 4 and hence every line quotient to have degree at least 6. For quotient degree 6, the kernel has degree 4. Four sections force the sum of the section dimensions of kernel and quotient to be at least 4. The relevant higher-section line-bundle loci with negative Brill-Noether number are empty on a general curve, leaving only two incidence products, each of dimension 4. Their tensor-product images therefore have dimension at most 4 in the six-dimensional degree-10 Picard variety, so a general determinant avoids them.
residual_risks: The result is only for stable bundles, general curves and general determinants.
Quotient degree at least 7 is untouched.

final_claim: On a general genus-6 curve with a general degree-10 determinant, no stable rank-two bundle with at least four sections admits a line-bundle quotient of degree at most 6.
limitations: General curve and general determinant only; special determinants can behave differently.
